To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a translation approach can provide portability for ontologies and that a declarative, representational ontology can be used to support translation.

a translation mechanism for portable specifications of shared knowledge can be built by defining a set of idioms in a declarative language, translating idioms to specialized representations using a set of transformation rules, and using the translation system itself to define the set of idioms.
the translation approach to portable ontologies is a viable approach to the problem of sharing ontologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a formalism that is expressive and flexible enough to capture the variety of knowledge representation techniques that have been developed, yet is also amenable to translation into a variety of specialized representations.
the development and use of ontologies for representing knowledge.
how to support the reuse of ontologies, and the sharing of knowledge represented by ontologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the translation approach to ontology portability has been successful.
the approach to portability described here is not a complete solution.
the Ontolingua system is an important step toward a general mechanism for defining, sharing and reusing knowledge representations, but that it is not yet complete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing an ontology of ontologies.

we have developed a system that supports the sharing and reuse among AI systems of formally represented knowledge by providing a common vocabulary for representing that knowledge and a translation mechanism for translating the knowledge into specialized representations.

we are developing a language for specifying ontologies, called Ontolingua, and a system for translating Ontolingua into various representations, including frame systems and logic programming languages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a translation approach to portabilty is a promising way of addressing the portabilty problem, and that it is possible to build systems that can translate between representations in a principled way.
it is possible to define ontologies in a portable manner.
the translation approach to ontology portability is a viable alternative to the development of a single, universal representation for knowledge sharing.
